title: Sawtooth peering ICMP + TLS scratchpad
content:
Summary:
Short notes/brain dump while chasing intermittent TLS failures from Private deployment (customer-onprem VPC peered to Redwood transit VPC). Problem shows as TLS handshake timeouts and sporadic ECONNRESETs to external endpoints on port 443. ICMP measurements show non-monotonic TTL/ICMP unreachable patterns (hence 'sawtooth'). Suspect asymmetric routing or middlebox dropping large fragments, TTL-snat, or peering device rate-limiting ICMP/TCP.

Symptoms observed (from app + infra):
- App logs: frequent 10-30s TLS handshake timeouts to a subset of external hosts (third-party auth and telemetry endpoints).
- nginx upstream: "upstream prematurely closed connection" and occasional "SSL handshake failed (SSL: error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number)"
- Kernel: periodic "ICMP destination unreachable (frag needed)" entries on some worker nodes.
- End-to-end curl from pod sometimes succeeds, sometimes immediately returns "Connection reset by peer". Success rate correlates with time-of-day/traffic volume.

Timeline (quick):
- 2026-03-09: First reports from Canary environment, low volume.
- 2026-03-10: Incident escalated when a customer saw auth failures.
- 2026-03-11: Added packet captures and synthetic probes.
- 2026-03-12: Reproduced in lab with constrained MTU and peered path.

Commands I ran (note: interface names redacted):
- ip route get 8.8.8.8
- traceroute -n -T -p 443 --mtu 8.8.8.8
- tcptraceroute 8.8.8.8 443
- mtr -r -w -c 50 3rd.party.endpoint.com
- sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/peer.pcap host 3rd.party.endpoint.com and port 443
- sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 'icmp or (tcp port 443 and (tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0))'
- curl -v --resolve "3rd.party.endpoint.com:443:203.0.113.12" https://3rd.party.endpoint.com/health --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30
- openssl s_client -connect 203.0.113.12:443 -servername 3rd.party.endpoint.com -tls1_2 -msg -debug
- iptables -t nat -L -n; nft list table inet filter || true
- sysctl net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc
- sudo ethtool -k eth0 | sed -n '1,80p'

Representative outputs (snippets):
- curl: "* Connected to 203.0.113.12 (203.0.113.12) port 443 (#0)\n* TLS 1.2 connection error: "; then "Recv failure: Connection reset by peer"
- openssl s_client: many lines of record layer errors: "ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert internal error" then EOF.
- tcpdump: see repeated ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) for MSS ~1400, but packets are <1400. Also intermittent ICMP type 3 code 1 (host unreachable) from a hop in the transit VPC.
- traceroute: hop 4 shows RTT spikes then disappears for 3/50 probes (mtr shows sawtooth RTT graph).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) MTU/PMTU interaction + middlebox rewriting causing TLS record fragmentation leading to handshake failure when PMTU path discovery blocked (ICMP filtered by firewall). Evidence: ICMP frag-needed observed; sysctl ip_no_pmtu_disc=0 on nodes; intermittent frag-needed means an intermediate device tries to signal but reply path broken.
2) Asymmetric routing at peering edge causing return path to go through different firewall that rate-limits or drops TCP with unknown state -> resets. Evidence: host unreachable ICMP from transit hop and correlation with time of day.
3) NAT or stateful firewall in customer-onprem peering that expires state earlier under load, causing server to receive SYN but client gets reset. Evidence: SYN reaches remote (tcpdump on remote shows SYN), but client sees RST.
4) SNI-stripping/transparent proxy doing TLS interception and failing for certain ALPN combinations (http/2). Evidence: ssl errors reference TLSv1 alerts; openssl s_client with -servername sometimes shows immediate alert.
5) DNS TTL mismatch or stale routes: some probes resolved to IPv6 vs IPv4 alternation; ephemeral failures when answer flips. Evidence: occasional AAAA answers in dig +short and curl using IPv6 failing.

Experiments / follow-ups we ran or should run:
- Re-run curl with --ipv4-only to see if failures tied to v6. (Done: decreased failures but not gone.)
- Force PMTU discovery off/on: sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=1 (disable) and retest. (Result: handshake failures decreased in lab but need longer window.)
- Increase MTU on PEER interface and on our node to test fragmentation avoidance. (Lab where MTU increased to 9000 -> stable.)
- From transit side, capture both directions to check for asymmetric path: tcpdump on peer router + our host simultaneously.
- Add temporary iptables rule to drop ICMP frag-needed replies to see how path reacts (simulate firewall blocking).
- Test with openssl s_client -keylogfile to debug TLS record fragmentation boundary.

Mitigations applied so far:
- Narrowed Canary to IPv4-only egress for the customer routes for 24h window.
- Added defensive retry around TLS handshake in SDK with backoff for 2 minutes.
- Engaged peering ops to review route tables and ACLs for transit VPC.

Notes for oncall / runbook actions:
- If customer reports "connection reset" pattern, check mtr for sawtooth RTT and tcpdump for ICMP frag-needed.
- Use: sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/handshake.pcap host <remote> and port 443 for at least 120s.
- Query route table: aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters "Name=tag:Name,Values=peer-transit" and correlate with BGP advertised routes (if applicable).
- If frag-needed present and we observe fragmentation, consider temporary MTU increase on worker ENIs and ask peering partner to allow ICMP type 3 code 4.

Open action items / owners:
- Samir: collect transit VPC tcpdumps for same time window as node pcap (ENG-5872).
- Networking: verify peering device MTU and ICMP rate limits (owner: network-ops).
- Platform: add PMTU diagnostic flag to canary config to force/disable DF bit for a run.
- Security: check any transparent proxies / TLS inspection appliances in customer path (owner: security-ops).

References / useful commands (for next run):
- curl -v --ipv4 --interface <pod-if> --resolve "host:443:<ip>" https://host/
- openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername host -tls1_2 -msg -debug
- sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/p.pcap 'icmp or tcp port 443'
- mtr -r -c 100 host
- iptables -t mangle -L -v; nft list ruleset

Conclusion (working theory):
Most likely root cause is interaction of PMTU discovery and peering middlebox behavior (ICMP being rate-limited or path asymmetry). Under load, fragmentation/DF interplay causes TLS records to be truncated or require retransmit; middlebox drops or returns unreachable which manifests as RST/handshake failures. Will validate by reproducing with controlled MTU/PMTU toggles and by getting coordinated captures from the peering device.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc minimal; paste important pcap offsets + packet hex for postmortem. Save final root cause and remediation steps to Confluence and link to ENG-5872.
